title: Ines and the Songbook
premise: Ines Dravenmoor, a lighthouse keeper's granddaughter who writes romance novels under a false name, inherits a half-share of a stubborn orchard she never knew her grandmother owned. The other half belongs to Silas, the man whose name she once erased from her life and her manuscripts a decade ago. Forced to share the deed through one growing season, they discover their families' histories are entangled in an old injustice the orchard's previous owner buried. When a developer's claim threatens to expose everything, Ines must choose between protecting her anonymity and testifying to the truth. They finally speak the rehearsed sentence at the vineyard's first harvest, choosing each other and justice over the safety of staying invisible.
about_author: Petra Oyelaran is a former land surveyor who spent years walking property lines along the northern coast before turning to fiction. She writes about inheritance, stubborn ground, and the people who learn that love cannot be filed away.

chapters.title: The Deed That Wouldn't Die
chapters.summary: Ines, sorting her late grandmother's papers in the lighthouse cottage, discovers an orchard deed bearing two names: her own family's and one she hasn't spoken aloud in ten years—Silas. Her POV. The emotional beat is dread disguised as curiosity; she almost burns the document but can't.

chapters.title: A Man Made of Weather
chapters.summary: Silas arrives at the orchard expecting sole possession and finds Ines already there, measuring fence lines. His POV reveals he has read every novel she published under her pen name and recognized himself in them. The beat is wounded tenderness beneath hostile small talk.

chapters.title: Terms of Coexistence
chapters.summary: They draft a brittle agreement: split the season, share nothing else. Ines's POV as she catalogs his habits like research for a villain. But a letter from the orchard's former owner surfaces, hinting the land was taken unjustly from a third family. Beat: unease compounding attraction.

chapters.title: What the Trees Remember
chapters.summary: Working the spring pruning together, they find carved initials inside the oldest apple tree—three names, not two. Silas's POV; he admits his grandfather once worked this land and was cheated of it. The beat is shared grief softening old blame.

chapters.title: The Developer's Letter
chapters.summary: A development company claims the deed is void due to a decades-old clerical fraud—and offers both of them money to walk away quietly. Ines's POV. Taking the money would erase the third family's claim forever. Beat: temptation sharpening into moral clarity.

chapters.title: Manuscripts and Confessions
chapters.summary: Ines finds Silas reading her unpublished manuscript hidden in the farmhouse—the one about them. His POV as she finally admits why she wrote him out of her life: fear that loving someone visible would cost her the anonymity she hid behind after a public scandal. Beat: raw exposure.

chapters.title: Harvest Eve
chapters.summary: On the eve of first harvest, the developer files suit, forcing a hearing that will require testimony under Ines's real name. Her POV, spiraling between flight and fight while Silas quietly gathers evidence of the original fraud. Beat: terror crystallizing into resolve.

chapters.title: The Sentence Rehearsed
chapters.summary: Climax. At the hearing, Ines testifies publicly, surrendering her pen name and exposing the land fraud. Outside the courthouse, before witnesses and cameras, she says the sentence rehearsed for a decade: that she loved him then and loves him still. Silas's POV. Beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: First Pressing
chapters.summary: The court restores the third family's descendants as co-owners; the four parties press the first cider together. Ines's POV, watching power redistribute itself willingly rather than by force. Beat: quiet joy, justice tasting like tart fruit.

chapters.title: Ines and the Songbook
chapters.summary: Epilogue. Ines publishes a new novel under her own name, dedicated to the three names in the tree. Silas reads it aloud in the orchard at dusk. Her POV closing the frame: love no longer past tense, identity no longer hidden. Beat: full-circle peace.
